newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Parade accident mars Lunar New Year in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Parade accident mars Lunar New Year in Hong Kong.

text.p: A float in a Lunar New Year's day parade plunged into a crowd of onlookers in Hong Kong on Friday, killing a British woman and injuring 31 others.

The float, organised by the Better Hong Kong Foundation, crashed through barriers and onto a pavement in the territory's busy Tsim Sha Tsui shopping and tourist district before swerving back onto the road where it stopped.
Scores of police worked frantically to rescue those trapped underneath the truck, finally tipping the vehicle on its side.
A British female tourist was reported dead on arrival at hospital. Two other people were seriously injured, one of them a policeman who tried to stop the float running over two children.
The dead woman was identified as B.A. Stevens, 45, from Yorkshire, England.
Police said they were investigating the cause of the accident, an inauspicious start to the Year of the Ox, but said the truck's driver had high levels of carbon monoxide in his blood.
This would indicate banners and decorations festooning the truck may have blocked the vehicle's exhaust pipe.
Friday's parade was the largest on record, with 23 floats and more than 20 performing groups from around the world celebrating Hong Kong's last Lunar New Year under British rule.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
